holidays.name: National Tequila Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a glass (or a salt-rimmed shot) to the famous agave spirit, whether you sip it neat, shake it into a margarita, or stir it into a Paloma.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food and drink holiday that grew popular in the United States in the 2010s, promoted largely by bars, restaurants, and liquor brands.
holidays.funFact: True tequila can only be made from blue Weber agave, and it must come from specific regions of Mexico, mainly the state of Jalisco. The agave plant takes around 7 to 10 years to mature.

holidays.name: National Thermos Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the humble vacuum flask that keeps your coffee scalding and your lemonade icy for hours, defying the laws of lukewarm.
holidays.origin: Celebrated on July 24 in the U.S. as an informal observance honoring the vacuum flask, which was invented by Scottish scientist Sir James Dewar in 1892 and later commercialized by German glassblowers.
holidays.funFact: Dewar never patented his invention, so he earned no money from it. 'Thermos' was originally a brand name, but it became a generic term, and the company lost exclusive trademark rights in the U.S. in 1963.

holidays.name: International Self-Care Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to looking after yourself, from taking a nap to getting a checkup to doing something that makes you feel human again, with no guilt allowed.
holidays.origin: Established by the International Self-Care Foundation, which chose July 24 (7/24) to symbolize that self-care should happen 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
holidays.funFact: The date was picked as a numerical pun: 7/24 stands for 'seven days a week, twenty-four hours a day', which makes it one of the few holidays whose date doubles as its slogan.

holidays.name: National Drive-Thru Day
holidays.description: A salute to the convenience of ordering a burger through a speaker and receiving it through a window, all without putting on real pants.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance in the U.S. celebrating the drive-thru, which rose with car culture. Red's Giant Hamburg in Springfield, Missouri, is often credited with an early drive-thru window in 1947.
holidays.funFact: Drive-thru lanes boomed during the 2020 pandemic, when many restaurants saw most of their sales come through that little window.

holidays.name: Amelia Earhart Day (Observed Around This Time) / National Cousins Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the cousins in your life: the first partners in crime, secret-keepers, and reluctant playmates at every family reunion.
holidays.origin: National Cousins Day is an informal observance in the U.S. on July 24, created to honor the close family bond cousins share.
holidays.funFact: Cousins are often called 'built-in best friends' because they share grandparents, family stories, and usually the same embarrassing childhood photos.
